things.name: the Orangery
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, for himself, with James Clephan as clerk of works (about 1835 in the listing; 1838–1839 in a Historic England research report)

things.name: the Archer Pavilion
things.who: designed by Thomas Archer for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; the Great Room painted by Hauduroy in 1712

things.name: the Pavilion's painted Great Room
things.who: painted in trompe-l'œil by Hauduroy, who signed it 'Hauduroy pinxit 1712'

things.name: the repair of the Pavilion's lead dome
things.who: carried out by English Heritage to stop rain reaching the painted ceiling

things.name: the 'river' canals
things.who: dug for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; reshaped in 1758–1760 by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke

things.name: Capability Brown's reshaping of the canals
things.who: carried out by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke

things.name: the Capability Brown column
things.who: attributed to the architect Edward Stevens; dated 1760 in the listing, but Historic England's 2018 research suggests about 1769–1771

things.name: the Bath House
things.who: designed by Edward Stevens for Jemima, Marchioness Grey

things.name: the Bath House Cascade
things.who: built with the Bath House, over the spring head

things.name: the lead water pipes to the Bath House
things.who: ordered by the estate agent after wooden pipes kept failing in the boggy ground

things.name: the filling-in of the Bath House's bath
things.who: ordered by Earl de Grey after hot and cold baths were fitted in the old house

things.name: the 1960s restoration of the Bath House
things.who: carried out by the Ministry of Public Building and Works; it re-thatched the dressing room and dug out and rebuilt the bath

things.name: the pump that recirculates water to the Cascade
things.who: installed by the Ministry's engineers, as the Bath House spring had dried up

things.name: the raising of Old Park Weir
things.who: raised 6–10 inches in concrete to hold more water for the research institute's irrigation

things.name: the brewhouse, horse pump house and fire-engine house
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, with James Clephan as clerk of works

people.name: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown
people.who: the most famous English landscape designer of the 18th century, who reshaped the boundary canals in 1758–1760
events: began work at Wrest for Jemima and Philip Yorke
became the King's Master Gardener at Hampton Court

people.name: Thomas Archer
people.who: the architect of the Archer Pavilion
events: began the Archer Pavilion at Wrest

people.name: Louis-Philippe
people.who: King of the French 1830–1848, who sold Wrest its orange trees
events: was overthrown and fled to England

people.name: Edward Stevens
people.who: the architect of the Bath House, a pupil of Sir William Chambers
events: began the Bath House at Wrest

people.name: Jemima, Marchioness Grey
people.who: the granddaughter and heir of Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; wife of Philip Yorke, who became 2nd Earl of Hardwicke in 1764
events: inherited Wrest when her grandfather died

people.name: Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey
people.who: the owner who built the present house and the Orangery; nephew of Amabel, Countess de Grey, from whom he inherited Wrest
events: became the first President of the Institute of British Architects
filled in the Bath House's bath
